pr_body:
The functions EVP_PKEY_get_raw_private_key and EVP_PKEY_get_raw_public_key fail with a NULL pointer deref if you pass a provider key to them. This also highlighted that EVP_PKEY_new_raw_private_key and EVP_PKEY_new_raw_public_key do not create provider side keys as you might expect.

This PR fixes both of those issues. Along the way a number of other issues were highlighted.

This is WIP because the tests are failing. At least one of those failures (possibly all of them) are because EVP_PKEY_cmp is not working with ECX provider side keys.

Fixes #11627
pr_comments:
> I had no time yet to review, but I wanted to start asking if we could also add a test for THESE new APIs so that we can catch further problems also with other key types?

Of course. We already had some tests for the non-libctx versions so I extended them to test both variants.

All feedback responded to and updates applied. I have rebased to resolve some conflicts with master and added some commits to deal with the test failures.

This is now out of WIP. Please take another look.
There are at least 3 different travis errors.
Fixups pushed addressing the feedback above. Hopefully should also fix the Travis issues.
This pull request is ready to merge

Unfortunately there was a conflict with master in ecx_meth.c - updated and force pushed.

@slontis please can you reconfirm?

issue_context.title: NULL dereference in EVP_PKEY_get_raw_private_key with provider side keys
issue_context.body:
When EVP_PKEY_get_raw_private_key or EVP_PKEY_get_raw_public_key is called with a provider side key, there is a NULL dereference.

pkey->ameth for provider side keys is NULL:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/crypto/evp/p_lib.c#L384

A check for NULL could be added:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/11628
comments: This highlighted a whole heap of problems with ECX provider keys. My fix for this issue and other related ones in #11635.

review_comments:
Will this actually work as an octet string???
ecx is the only one that uses octet string for both priv and pub.
ec uses BN for priv.
dsa and dh use BN for both.
Ahh I see the docs say only weird types are used :)
Yes...this is for raw keys which are always just a string of bytes.
Engine API's need to be ifdef
Should then functions be passing a property_query string also?

This is definitely a non-trivial task. The problem is that this code is called provider side. If we're going to use the property query here then we'd have to pass it through as an OSSL_PARAM, and presumably have an `ecx_set_params` implementation in order to be able to associate that query with the key in some way. I suspect this problem is bigger than just ECX (we're quite inconsistent about where we pass both a libctx and propq and where we just pass a libctx) - so I suspect we're going to need to address that as a separate issue. Solving this in this case is straying quite far from my original scope for this PR - so I'd rather not try and deal with this here.
We pass property queries without the libctx in places.  KDF definitely but I think MAC too.
